chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said:

You have from your prayer only that portion for which you were attentive; so if you were negligent of all of it, or heedless of its performance, it is folded up and struck upon the face of its performer.
ai.seo_question: How does attentiveness affect the acceptance of prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes that the spiritual efficacy of salāt is contingent upon khushu' (attentiveness), a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of prayer for those with minor distractions. The metaphor of the prayer being 'folded and struck against the face' illustrates the tangible consequence of negligence, distinguishing between mere physical performance and true spiritual presence. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that while the prayer remains valid, its reward is directly proportional to the degree of mindfulness maintained throughout the ritual.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Al Fazeyl Bin Yasaar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both having said:

‘But rather, for you, from your Salāt is what you a devoted upon it, from it. So if all of it is (full of) imagination, or oblivion from its execution, it is diverted and its performer is struck with it upon his face’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said, ‘

Of your Salah (prayer) only that much is for you which you have performed with love. If one instills delusion in Salah (prayer) or omits it altogether, then such Salah (prayer) is rolled up and is struck against the face of its owner.’”
